title: Pate (slit drum)
summary: The pate is a small slit drum of Samoa, a carved block of hardwood with a narrow slit across its top. Struck with two thin sticks it gives a sharp, hollow beat that keeps the time for songs and dances, with a deeper stroke on one side of the slit and a higher one on the other.
howToPlay: The pate stands on a fine mat, seen from the front: the slit on its top, the carved band on its face.
Low is the left half of the slit, High the right half, Face the carved front and Edge the thin rim along the top.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the steady strokes on the low and high sides, then add the edge.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: The pate came to Samoa from other parts of Polynesia and became the drum that keeps the beat for choirs and dancers. A good player holds a steady pulse for a whole song and lets the dancers' movements follow it.
credits: Tradition: the Pate; patterns written for this game
